candidates.title: Draft restaurant order status messages

demandEvidence.chore: Connect restaurant order systems with customer notifications and delivery updates, including order confirmations, delivery assignments, and failed notifications.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to understand how n8n can help connect restaurant order systems, customer notifications, and delivery updates.

experimentPlan.output: A review queue of concise draft messages for fictional order confirmations, delivery assignments, status updates, and notification failures.
inputs: Fictional order ID and restaurant label
Fictional order status and delivery assignment
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one fictional order event to a manually started test run.
steps: Accept a fictional order event in a fixed sample format.
Check that its status and delivery assignment use allowed sample values.
Select a proposed message template for that event type.
Draft a short customer update using only supplied fields.
Flag missing fields or a failure state for human review.
Show the draft and event side by side for approval.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed set of fictional events, verify each draft repeats the supplied order status and assignment accurately, flags missing values, and never sends a message.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies fictional test records and approved wording, checks every draft and failure flag, and authorizes any later live integration or message sending.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents webhook receipt, restaurant system access, messaging integrations, retry behavior, or delivery.
The post does not establish field schemas, event frequency, commercial demand, or whether automated wording is acceptable.

ease.reason: A beginner can mock one status-to-message path with synthetic rows, but no supplied reference supports webhooks or messaging integrations.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: restaurant operators may pay to reduce manual order updates; this request proves neither purchase intent nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can draft confirmation and status messages from sample events; integrations, delivery and failure handling remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-draft loop is repeatable, but no implementation capability is documented and a person must verify and approve messages.

evidence.reason: The retained post span asks about order data, restaurant notifications, customer updates and failures, but supplies no field details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The retained post span states a concrete order-notification workflow, so I scoped a synthetic draft-only experiment. No matching implementation reference is supplied; the honest mean is below the threshold.

candidates.title: Check laboratory batch records against a schema

demandEvidence.chore: Automate handling and validation of high-frequency laboratory batch records in chemical manufacturing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: laboratory testing instruments generate high-frequency batch records that require automated

experimentPlan.output: A review queue listing fictional laboratory batch records that fail operator-defined required-field or value-range checks.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a small fictional batch-record file to a manually started validation run.
steps: Load fictional records in one fixed table format.
Check each row for the operator-defined required fields.
Compare numeric sample values with operator-supplied ranges.
Mark each row as complete, missing data, or outside the supplied range.
Produce a review queue with the failed rule and original sample value.
Ask an operator to verify flags and amend the sample schema.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Run a fixed fictional file containing known missing fields and out-of-range values; verify every seeded issue appears with the correct row and rule, and valid rows are not flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies and approves the fictional schema and ranges, reviews every flag, and decides any real batch disposition; this experiment must not process production or patient data.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports file ingestion, numeric validation, batch-record storage, instrument connectivity, or n8n execution.
The retained excerpt does not identify measurement fields, validation rules, review frequency, buyer intent, or payment.
Synthetic checks do not establish production reliability, regulatory compliance, or tax correctness.

ease.reason: A beginner can define a small synthetic table check, but no supplied reference supports file intake or validation automation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: chemical manufacturers may pay for batch-record checks; this post establishes a chore, not purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can check fictional required fields and supplied ranges; actual instrument formats and production rules are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A proposed repeatable row-checking loop is bounded, but no implementation capability is documented and an operator must review all flags.

evidence.reason: The retained text identifies high-frequency laboratory batch records needing automation, but gives no concrete fields, rules, examples, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The fresh literal excerpt supports automating laboratory batch records, so I assessed a narrow fictional schema-checking experiment. No supplied implementation reference supports execution, and task fields and rules are absent; the honest provisional mean is below six.
